input.question: Why do we have to consciencley swallow a liquid, what is inhibiting it from merely sliding down our throats?
input.ground_truth: Because normally, our airways are open unconsciously, with the epiglottis standing strait up, allowing air to flow in and out. When we swollow, the muscles in our throat push on the epiglottis, closing the larynx, guiding the food to the esophagus and stomach. So, if we were to allow saliva or other fluids to just slide down, without swallowing, it wouldn't be guided into the stomach, it would be guided down our bronchi and lungs, since the airway wouldn't close. Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why do we have to consciencley swallow a liquid, what is inhibiting it from merely sliding down our throats?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a little straw and you put some juice in it. If you just let the juice sit, it will slowly slide down by itself, right? But when you drink, your body helps the juice go down faster by squeezing it with your throat muscles. This is called "swallowing." 

If you don’t help by swallowing on purpose, the juice might just sit at the top of your mouth and not go down right away. Your body has to "tell" your throat to squeeze and push the juice down. That’s why you have to swallow **consciously**—so you can help the juice go where it needs to go! If you didn’t help, it might feel weird or make you cough. 

So, swallowing helps things go down the right way!
